startup.name: Kaizen
startup.one_liner: Digital employee that gets patients into care faster
startup.description: AI agent that processes referrals, verifies insurance benefits, manages prior authorizations and handles provider credentialing across the systems healthcare teams already use. Paid by provider groups per task or seat, replacing back office staff and outsourcers.

yc_acceptance.basis: YC publishes no acceptance rate; the working prior is about 1 percent with a band of 0.6 to 2 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md). This company is already in the batch named in the input, so the number is for completeness only. Six person team with a concrete, paid problem in healthcare operations and an AI native wedge fits YC priorities; crowded by funded rivals, so a modest lift to about 1.5 percent. Already in the batch.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Healthcare administrative automation is crowded with funded rivals in prior authorization, intake and credentialing, so YC could say the wedge is not specific, that healthcare integrations are a slog and that web automation of payer portals is fragile. YC may also see healthcare administration automation as overfunded in 2025, with many teams applying for prior authorization and intake, so a six person team with no stated customers needs a sharp single workflow and early paid pilots to stand out.

narrative.headline: A hot AI healthcare back office wedge with real demand but heavy competition, so the window odds sit near the cohort anchor.
narrative.general_summary: Kaizen sells an AI digital employee for healthcare referrals, benefits checks, prior authorizations and credentialing. The 19.3 month window is long enough for a typical seed, and the B2B and AI cohorts show about half of companies ever raising a seed. A six person team in a hot category does not justify a lift per the winners test, so the odds are near 38 percent and say little about this company versus others in the batch. Healthcare back office automation is a hot category, and the six person team has a concrete paid task, but the input shows no customers. The scored numbers are window specific and anchored on older cohorts, and the remaining risk is mostly execution and timing rather than the idea alone.
